AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.SemanticAmbiguity: Your requirement contains unclear or subjective terms that may be understood differently.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.ScopeAmbiguity: Your requirement has unclear boundaries, so it is not clear exactly what is included.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.ActorAmbiguity: Your requirement does not clearly identify who should perform this action.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.AcceptanceAmbiguity: Your requirement does not clearly explain how we can decide whether the result is successful.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.DependencyAmbiguity: Your requirement depends on another person, process, system, or event that is not clearly specified.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.PriorityAmbiguity: Your requirement does not clearly indicate how important or urgent it is.
AMBIGUITY_INITIAL_PROMPTS.TechnicalAmbiguity: Your requirement mentions a technical operation without clearly specifying what is expected.

SemanticAmbiguity: Some words or phrases in your requirement are too general or subjective.
Different people may understand these words or phrases differently.
Words such as 'quickly', 'regularly', 'reasonable', or 'appropriate' do not provide a specific expectation.
ScopeAmbiguity: The main purpose of the requirement is understandable, but its boundaries are unclear.
It may not be clear exactly how far the requirement should apply.
It may be unclear which users, activities, situations, or features are included.
ActorAmbiguity: The requirement describes an action, but it does not clearly identify who is responsible for performing it.
Words such as 'user', 'staff', or 'employee' may refer to different people or roles.
The responsible person or role should be clearly identified.
AcceptanceAmbiguity: The requirement explains what should happen, but does not clearly explain how success will be determined.
It may be difficult to decide whether the completed feature actually meets the requirement.
Clear conditions or expected results are needed so everyone can agree when the requirement is complete.
DependencyAmbiguity: The requirement relies on something else, such as another person, process, system, approval, or event.
It is not clear what needs to happen before this requirement can be completed.
It may also be unclear what should happen after the dependent activity is completed.
PriorityAmbiguity: The requirement does not clearly indicate how important or urgent it is.
It is not clear how this requirement should be prioritized compared with other requirements.
This can make it difficult to decide which requirement should be handled first.
TechnicalAmbiguity: The requirement mentions a technical solution or operation without enough detail.
It may be unclear how the expected technical behavior should work.
Different developers may therefore implement the requirement in different ways.

SemanticAmbiguity: What exactly do you mean by this term or phrase?
Could you provide a specific example of what you expect?
Can you replace this general term with a specific value, condition, or time?
What specific result would you consider acceptable?
How would you describe this requirement so that everyone understands it in the same way?
ScopeAmbiguity: What exactly should this feature include?
Who should this requirement apply to?
Are there any users, activities, or situations that should be excluded?
Are there any limits or conditions on when this feature should be used?
What should the system do outside the scope of this requirement?
ActorAmbiguity: Which user role or staff member is responsible for this activity?
Who should be allowed to use this feature?
Can more than one role perform this action?
Who should be responsible when this action requires approval?
AcceptanceAmbiguity: How will you know that this requirement has been successfully completed?
What specific result should the system produce?
What conditions must be satisfied for this requirement to be considered successful?
Are there specific numbers, limits, time periods, or quality standards that must be met?
Can you give an example of a successful result?
DependencyAmbiguity: Does this requirement depend on another person, process, or system?
What needs to happen before this action can take place?
What should happen after this action is completed?
Which external system, service, or person is involved?
What should happen if the required person, process, or system is unavailable?
PriorityAmbiguity: How important is this requirement compared with the other requirements?
Should this requirement be completed before the others?
Is there a specific deadline for this requirement?
